reference_memory.normal_pattern: The normal pattern is a piecewise-constant, stepwise-decaying signal with a dominant downward trend composed of discrete, abrupt level shifts (steps) rather than smooth slopes. The periodicity is not sinusoidal; instead, the cadence is defined by the spacing and magnitude of these steps, which recur roughly every ~30–50 points in the robust-standardized domain. Stability is high within each plateau (near-zero roughness and curvature), but the overall series is non-stationary due to the monotonic drift. Amplitude variation across candidates is large in raw units (e.g., 12,000 vs. <1), but after robust standardization, the normalized amplitude (90th percentile range) is modest (≤0.83), indicating that the underlying process has bounded variability relative to its local scale. Peaks and troughs are sharp, rectangular transitions—no rounded extrema—occurring at step edges; troughs are deeper and more frequent than peaks. Noise is negligible: all profiles show near-zero MAD (<0.38) and no high-frequency jitter except for minor micro-steps near the end of candidates 2 and 3, likely measurement quantization or sensor resolution effects. Acceptable variation includes: (i) number of steps (3–6 visible in 256-point windows), (ii) step height (typically −0.05 to −0.1 per step), (iii) plateau duration (variable, 10–40 points), and (iv) presence of rare micro-oscillations (≤2 small wiggles) near low levels. Candidate 0 is an outlier: it is perfectly flat (zero slope, zero MAD), suggesting either a dead sensor segment or extreme smoothing—this does not reflect the typical operational behavior seen in the other three candidates.

reference_profiles.description: Perfectly flat line at robust-standardized value ≈12000 (raw-scale constant); zero variation, zero slope, zero MAD; no steps, no noise, no dynamics; appears artificially static or truncated.

Two-level step: high plateau (~12000) for ~120 points, then abrupt drop to near-zero; strong negative slope per point (−47) due to single large jump; otherwise flat segments; no intermediate steps or noise.

Multi-step descent over 256 points: ~6–7 discrete downward steps of ~−0.05 to −0.1 each; plateaus of varying length; ends with minor micro-oscillations (2–3 tiny wiggles) near −0.5; low MAD (0.15), stable within plateaus.

Extended 5-cycle window showing smoother multi-step decay over 427 points: ~8–9 steps, similar step sizes to candidate 2; includes more micro-oscillations (3–4 small wiggles) near mid-to-low levels; slightly higher MAD (0.26); consistent morphology with candidate 2 but longer context confirms recurrence.

reference_memory.selection_guidance: Prefer candidates 2 and 3 for query matching: their stepwise decay with micro-wiggles defines the consensus normal behavior. Use candidate 3 for queries >300 points (to capture full cycle structure); use candidate 2 for 250–300 point queries (optimal balance of detail and compactness). Avoid candidate 0 unless the query is perfectly flat and long-duration—treat such matches as suspicious. Candidate 1 is useful only for detecting single-abrupt-drop anomalies; if a query shows one large drop without subsequent steps, compare against candidate 1—but verify against candidates 2/3 to rule out truncation.
